name: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co., Limited (宁德时代新能源科技股份有限公司)
summary: BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: CATL holds both global #1 battery positions (EV and ESS) but its storage lead is narrowing; we assess the sodium-ion and battery-swap pushes are deliberate moves to open post-lithium and infrastructure revenue before rivals close the cell gap. BACKGROUND: CATL is the world's largest lithium-ion battery manufacturer, spun out of ATL in 2011 and listed in Shenzhen (June 2018) and Hong Kong (May 2025 — the HK$41B raise was the world's largest IPO of 2025, with ~90% of proceeds earmarked for the Debrecen, Hungary plant). It supplies EV batteries to most global automakers and utility/C&I energy storage systems worldwide, with the storage business (TENER line) now its fastest-growing segment: ESS revenue grew 87.5% YoY in H1 2026 to nearly 20% of total revenue.
ecosystemRole: No. 1 in global EV power batteries for nine consecutive years (39.2% of 1,187 GWh installed in 2025, SNE Research) and No. 1 in energy-storage batteries for five consecutive years — though the ESS lead narrowed in 2025 (company-reported ESS share 30.4%, down from 36.5%; Benchmark estimates ~20% with Hithium and EVE at ~12% each). ESS battery sales: 93 GWh (2024) → 121 GWh (2025). Anchor storage deployment: sole BESS supplier (19 GWh of TENER) for Masdar's US$6B 5.2 GW round-the-clock solar+storage project in Abu Dhabi — the largest single BESS order to date.

productsAndServices.name: Passenger EV batteries (Qilin & Shenxing families)
productsAndServices.description: Core business — 74.7% of FY2025 revenue; power battery sales 541 GWh in 2025 (+42%), global EV battery share 39.9% in H1 2026 (SNE Research). Two flagship lines refreshed at the April 2026 Super Tech Day: (1) Qilin — CTP (cell-to-pack) NMC packs; 3rd-gen Qilin (Apr 2026) charges at an equivalent 10C with 15C peak, hits 600 Wh/L / 280 Wh/kg, and a 125 kWh pack delivers >1,000 km while weighing 625 kg (255 kg lighter than a comparable LFP pack); a track version peaks at 3,000 kW discharge; the Qilin Condensed Battery variant reaches 350 Wh/kg / 760 Wh/L for 1,500 km executive sedans. (2) Shenxing — superfast-charging LFP for the mass market: 2nd-gen (Apr 2025) was the world's first LFP pack combining 800 km range with a 12C peak rate (1.3 MW peak, ~2.5 km of range per second; 5–80% in 15 min at −10°C); Shenxing Pro (IAA, Sept 2025) localizes the line for Europe in long-life (758 km WLTP, 12-year/1M-km) and superfast (683 km WLTP, 12C, 478 km in 10 min) variants with NP 3.0 no-fire thermal-runaway protection; 3rd-gen Shenxing (Apr 2026) reaches equivalent 10C/15C peak — 10–80% in 3 min 44 s and 20–98% in ~9 min at −30°C, with >90% capacity after 1,000 cycles.
highlights: Customers include Tesla, BMW, Mercedes-Benz, VW, Toyota, Hyundai, and the major Chinese OEMs
No. 1 in global EV power batteries for nine consecutive years; 39.9% share in H1 2026 vs BYD's 14.4%
Condensed-matter (semi-solid-state) chemistry at 500 Wh/kg completed maiden-flight validation on a 4-tonne aircraft — the aviation-grade ceiling of the passenger roadmap
productsAndServices.positioning: Defends the top spot on spec leadership across every chemistry and price band simultaneously — 15C-peak NMC (Qilin 3) against high-nickel packs from LG Energy Solution, Samsung SDI and SK On; 12C→15C LFP (Shenxing) against BYD's in-house Blade line; condensed-matter density no competitor has productized — rather than competing on price alone.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct multi-year cell/pack supply agreements with OEMs; in access-restricted markets (US) the same IP is monetized via the LRS licensing line instead of cell exports.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Global passenger-EV OEMs from premium (Qilin NMC / Condensed) to mass market (Shenxing LFP); European OEMs served increasingly from the Hungary (Debrecen) plant build-out.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 3rd-gen Qilin and Shenxing vehicle launches from late 2026; Qilin Condensed pack productization; 500 Wh/kg condensed-matter aviation battery targeted at 8-tonne aircraft in the 2027–28 window.

productsAndServices.name: Hybrid & multi-chemistry packs (Freevoy)
productsAndServices.description: Freevoy Super Hybrid battery line for EREVs and PHEVs — the fastest-growing vehicle segment in China. 2nd-gen Freevoy (Apr 2026): LFP version gives 500 km all-electric range with equivalent-10C charging at 230 Wh/kg (+20% vs conventional LFP); NCM version gives 600 km electric / ~2,000 km combined range with 1,500 kW full-charge output. The companion dual-power architecture (Apr 2025) splits the pack into two independent energy zones that can mix chemistries (sodium+LFP for cold climates, LFP+LFP for cost, NCM pairings for range), with self-forming-anode technology claimed to raise volumetric energy density up to 60%.
productsAndServices.positioning: Aims at BYD's DM-i hybrid dominance by offering hybrid OEMs a longer-electric-range, faster-charging pack than typical PHEV batteries.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Chinese and global OEMs' EREV/PHEV programs.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Sodium-LFP dual-power configurations scale with the broader 2026 sodium deployment push.

productsAndServices.name: Commercial-vehicle batteries (Tectrans / Tianxing)
productsAndServices.description: Dedicated commercial-vehicle brand (launched July 2024) spanning light trucks, heavy trucks, buses, construction machinery and vessels. Tianxing II series (Jan 2026) included the world's first mass-production sodium-ion battery for commercial vehicles; the 8C superfast-charging LCV battery (July 2026) charges 20–80% in 6 min 48 s and to full in 8 min 56 s — refueling-time parity with gasoline — with a million-kilometre warranty.
highlights: First battery in its class with an 8C peak charging capability
30+ swap-ready truck models launched with FAW Jiefang, Shaanxi Auto and 10+ other OEMs on standardized swap blocks
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes with EVE Energy and CALB in commercial-vehicle cells; differentiates on charge speed plus the only nationwide charge-and-swap network purpose-built for freight.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Direct to truck/bus OEMs; batteries also deployed as swap blocks through the Qiji Energy network (battery-as-a-service).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Urban delivery and light commercial fleets, regional freight, cold-chain logistics, heavy-duty tractors, port/mining machinery, electric vessels.
productsAndServices.roadmap: 4,000 LCV-adapted integrated charge-and-swap stations targeted by end-2026 across ~190 cities.

productsAndServices.name: Utility-scale storage (TENER family)
productsAndServices.description: The fastest-growing business: ESS battery sales 93 GWh (2024) → 121 GWh (2025) → 125 GWh shipped in H1 2026 alone (27.1% global share, InfoLink/SNE via CnEVPost), and nearly 20% of group revenue in H1 2026 (+87.5% YoY). Three generations of grid product: TENER (Apr 2024) — the world's first mass-producible '5-year zero-degradation' container, 6.25 MWh per 20-ft unit at 430 Wh/L with >15,000 cycles; TENER Stack (May 2025) — 9 MWh from two stackable half-height containers (<36 t each, road-legal in ~99% of markets) on the 587 Ah LFP cell unveiled Apr 2025, improving volume utilization 45% vs a standard 20-ft container; TENER Sodium (June 2026) — the first field-validated sodium-ion BESS, 30+ MWh per modular configuration (the same architecture reaches 50 MWh with LFP cells).
highlights: 19 GWh Masdar Abu Dhabi order — largest single BESS order to date
TENER Sodium launch pipeline: 60 GWh HyperStrong (3-year), 5 GWh Alfen partnership, 2 GWh Solarpro agreement
IEEE693 seismic (magnitude-9) and category-5 hurricane compliance on TENER Stack; gas sensors trigger suppression 35% faster than prior generation
productsAndServices.positioning: Sets the density and warranty benchmarks the market chases: 6.25→9 MWh per footprint vs Tesla Megapack 3 (~5 MWh class), Samsung SDI SBB 1.5 (5.26 MWh, NCA) and BYD HaoHan (14.5 MWh flat-form unit); the 5-year zero-degradation claim is a bankability lever no major rival matches. Global ESS-cell rivals Hithium (10.0% H1 2026), EVE Energy and BYD are compressing the lead China-side, pushing CATL toward overseas projects and sodium differentiation.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Dual-track: cells to third-party integrators (historically including Tesla and Fluence) AND complete DC-block containers direct to developers, IPPs and EPCs under long-term supply agreements (e.g. Masdar).
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Utility-scale developers and IPPs, Middle East mega-projects, European grid operators, US market via cell supply where tariffs permit.
productsAndServices.roadmap: TENER Sodium first China deliveries Sept 2026 (~1 GWh cumulative by year-end), international deliveries from June 2027; storage durations configurable 1–8 h; 587 Ah cell ramping across the TENER fleet.

productsAndServices.name: C&I / modular storage (EnerOne, EnerD)
productsAndServices.description: EnerOne/EnerOne+ liquid-cooled outdoor LFP cabinets (280 Ah cells, ~372 kWh per cabinet) for C&I and modular utility builds; EnerD (2023) was the world's first mass-delivered 5 MWh 20-ft container, built on 314 Ah cells with CTP liquid-cooling 3.0 grouping — saving >20% floor space and ~15% construction work vs the 3.35 MWh generation. Both precede and complement TENER in global C&I and utility fleets.
productsAndServices.positioning: Competes in the crowded liquid-cooled-cabinet segment against Sungrow PowerTitan derivatives, EVE and Hithium C&I lines; wins on cell pedigree and global service network.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cells and cabinets via integrators, EPCs and distributors; cabinet-level sales into C&I projects.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Commercial & industrial behind-the-meter storage, smaller utility projects, markets where 20-ft mega-containers are impractical.

productsAndServices.name: Sodium-ion batteries (Naxtra)
productsAndServices.description: The industry's first mass-produced sodium-ion line (unveiled Apr 2025): the passenger-EV battery reaches 175 Wh/kg — the highest of any sodium-ion battery and comparable to LFP — with ~500 km range, >10,000 cycles, operation from −40°C to +70°C and 90% usable power at −40°C; the Naxtra 24V heavy-truck integrated start-stop battery cuts lifecycle cost ~61% vs lead-acid with an 8+ year life. First sodium-ion battery to pass China's GB 38031-2025 mandatory safety standard. Heavy-truck variant entered production June 2025; passenger-EV packs from December 2025, powering the world's first mass-production sodium-ion passenger car with Changan (Nevo A06).
highlights: Intrinsic-safety design removes combustion-supporting factors at the material level
Dec 2025 supplier conference: sodium scales across battery swap, passenger and commercial vehicles, and energy storage in 2026
productsAndServices.positioning: Years ahead of HiNa Battery and other sodium startups on scale, and hedges CATL against lithium-price spikes; cold-climate performance and thermal stability are the differentiation wedges vs its own LFP.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Cells/packs direct to OEMs; grid form factor sold as TENER Sodium; swap blocks planned.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Cold-climate EVs, entry-level passenger cars, heavy-truck electrics (start-stop), grid storage seeking 25–30-year asset life.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Large-scale multi-sector deployment through 2026; TENER Sodium global deliveries June 2027; second-generation sodium chemistry in development.

productsAndServices.name: Battery swap (Choco-Swap / EVOGO + Qiji Energy)
productsAndServices.description: Two standardized swap ecosystems. Passenger/light-duty (Choco-Swap, operated via EVOGO): standardized Choco-SEB blocks (20#/25#; the new #26 block announced Apr 2026 moves to an 800 V architecture, launching at 75 kWh) adopted by 11 automakers across 18 brands and 25 models; the network grew from 1,020 stations in 45 cities (end-2025) to its 2,000th station on June 30, 2026 (180 cities), targeting 3,000+ stations and 190+ cities by end-2026; China's first standardized light-truck swap ecosystem launched May 2026. Heavy-duty (Qiji Energy, launched June 2023): the 75# standardized swap block (May 2025) with ~305 stations operating and ~900 planned for 2026; J&T Express signed for swap services covering 5,000 heavy trucks (July 2026).
highlights: Sinopec partnership: 500+ co-built stations near-term, 10,000 medium-term with partners, 30,000 long-term ambition
Combined Choco + Qiji station count targeted to exceed 4,000 by end-2026 — approaching NIO's network built since 2018
100,000+ shared energy-replenishment facilities (charge + swap) targeted by end-2028
productsAndServices.positioning: Unlike NIO's single-brand network, CATL standardizes the swap block across many OEMs — the block, not the station, is the platform; scale + Sinopec's forecourt real estate are the moats.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: EVOGO/Qiji operate stations; batteries leased as battery-as-a-service (vehicle sold without battery); stations co-built with Sinopec and local partners.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Ride-hail and taxi fleets, mass-market passenger EVs, urban logistics light trucks, heavy-freight corridors ('eight horizontal, ten vertical' trunk network).
productsAndServices.roadmap: #26 800 V block first deliveries with larger capacities to follow; nationwide highway-corridor coverage (12 vertical / 11 horizontal) by end-2026; sodium-ion swap blocks planned.

productsAndServices.name: Skateboard chassis (CIIC / Bedrock)
productsAndServices.description: CATL Integrated Intelligent Chassis (CIIC) — a cell-to-chassis skateboard platform sold through subsidiary CAIT; the flagship Bedrock Chassis (Dec 2024) is marketed as the world's first 'ultra-safe' skateboard chassis. Avatr (Changan) is the first adopter; in May 2026 Togg (Turkey) signed the first overseas passenger-car mass-production deal for a Chinese skateboard chassis — three co-developed B-segment models, first mass production 2027. Earlier CIIC MoUs/partnerships include Neta (Hozon), VinFast, BAIC and a Changan Mazda co-development.
highlights: Chassis unit raised its first external financing in July 2025 — a step toward standalone platform economics
productsAndServices.positioning: Converts CATL from component supplier to platform provider: integrating pack and chassis captures more vehicle value and locks in cell demand; competes with OEM in-house platforms and contract-platform players rather than other cell makers.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Co-development and platform-licensing contracts via CAIT.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: Newer or smaller OEMs without full EV-platform R&D budgets; overseas national champions (Togg, VinFast); OEMs electrifying niche lines quickly.
productsAndServices.roadmap: First Togg model into mass production 2027; additional CIIC design-ins in negotiation.

productsAndServices.name: Technology licensing (LRS model)
productsAndServices.description: License-Royalty-Service deals monetize CATL IP in markets closed to Chinese investment: CATL supplies patent licenses, production technology, equipment and ramp-up services for a one-time fee plus per-unit royalties, without owning the plant. Flagship: Ford's US$3.5B BlueOval Battery Park Michigan (~20 GWh/yr LFP design capacity) — the first US plant making LFP cells for the mainstream consumer market — entered testing mid-2026 with market-ready cells due before end-2026, supported on-site by CATL engineers. Reported talks with GM (plant targeted ~2027) and roughly a dozen automakers in total; LRS-model capacity stood at ~139 GWh (~10% of CATL's operating + announced total) as of Nov 2024.
productsAndServices.positioning: Turns US restrictions (DoD 1260H listing, tariffs, IRA sourcing rules) from a wall into a royalty stream — where Korean rivals (LG, SK On, Samsung SDI) commit their own capital to US plants, CATL earns from IP with near-zero capex.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: License + royalty + service contracts with OEMs and battery makers.
productsAndServices.targetSegments: US and European automakers needing domestically produced, IRA-compliant LFP cells.
productsAndServices.roadmap: GM LFP plant ~2027 if concluded; additional LRS deals under discussion across the reported dozen-OEM pipeline.

productsAndServices.name: Battery recycling & materials (Brunp)
productsAndServices.description: Closed-loop recycling and cathode-materials subsidiary (Brunp Recycling) recovering lithium, nickel, cobalt and manganese from end-of-life packs and production scrap back into CATL's cathode supply chain; Brunp won two honors at the European Inventor Award 2026 for its directional-circulation recycling technology.

strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess CATL retains both global #1 positions (EV and ESS batteries) but the ESS lead is narrowing — company-reported share fell to 30.4% in 2025 from 36.5%, with Hithium and EVE at roughly 12% each per third-party estimates.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the sodium-ion line (Naxtra, TENER Sodium) is a post-lithium hedge competitors must now answer — launch-to-commercial-pipeline conversion took weeks, with European integrators carrying the projects while CATL sells the chemistry transition.

(Moderate confidence) We assess battery-swap (Qiji) has crossed from pilot to scaling network business — the 3,000-station/190-city end-2026 target appears credible given the network doubled in the first half of 2026.

(Moderate confidence) We assess the Hong Kong raise (~90% of proceeds to Debrecen) commits CATL to European localization ahead of EU content rules — supply-chain positioning rather than opportunistic financing.
